lectures.title: Time and Space Complexity of Binary Heap

cues.en: All right.
In this lecture we are going to look at big picture of time and space complexity in binary heap.
Now the first method is insert method.
Now we know that insert method takes a log n time complexity.
Because after inserting an element to the heap, we have to call heapify which may travel up to the
root.
And this is going to take logarithmic time relative to the number of the elements.
That's why the time complexity for insert method is or log n.
Now the space complexity is o one, because here an additional memory is not required to perform this
operation.
Now when it comes to the extract method, here again when we are removing the element from the root,
then we have to heapify the using Heapify down method, which is going to take logarithmic time because
it may traverse down to the leaf.
That's why it's going to be the whole time complexity.
Now here again the space complexity is o one, because an additional memory is not required to perform
this operation.
Now, when it comes to the Isempty method it's going to take a one time complexity and or one space
complexity, because here we are just checking the length of the array.
And based on that we are identifying if it is empty or not.
Then we have the size method.
So this is also the same operation because based on the length of the array that we have declared in
binary heap constructor, we are going to identify the size of the binary heap.
Then the next method is peek method.
Now the peek method is returning the top element from the binary heap, which is going to be the root.
So here we are returning it based on the index.
So we know that if we use the index to access the elements of the array, it's going to take or one
time and space.
Now the level or the traversal takes on time complexity.
Because in this case we have to visit each elements of the binary heap.
That's why if the number of the elements is n and the time complexity is going to be o n, now the space
complexity is O one, because here also an additional memory is not required.
We are just using the iteration over here.
That's why the space complexity is O one.
So with this lecture we have come to the end of this section.
So hopefully everything is clear about binary heap.
